description: Known gaps for desktop/tools/check_slice_symbol_closure.py. A gap listed here is accepted; a gap listed but no longer observed is stale and fails the gate (a partial run judges only the gaps its checks can observe). Every slice appends the gaps it knowingly leaves and removes the ones it closes. closedByEvidence says how firm the owner is: roadmap = that slice's roadmap text names the symbol; proposed = the gap author's inference, to be confirmed or reassigned by the slice owner; unassigned = no roadmap slice owns it. retiredSeeds are roadmap seeds a generated shim already defines; the gate fails if one loses its definer.

groups.reason: Policies upstream moved into core-data (data.model) that the pinned tree still keeps elsewhere or lacks (roadmap seeds: resolveVideoCardStatsTexts, resolveWatchLaterDisplayProgressState).
ForegroundSettleBudget is referenced by carried home archives and not declared (roadmap seed).
Instant-article symbols called by the carried favorite-search archive.

Instant-article symbols called by the carried favorite-search archive. Ownership of these symbols by rss-reader-page-repin is the gap author's inference: that slice's roadmap text does not name shouldAttemptInstantArticle. Its owner must confirm or reassign them when the slice is reached.

Windows desktop-wallpaper seed: SystemWallpaperSeed.kt reads the Android system accent palette (system_accent1_500, Android 12+). Windows has no such palette resource; the equivalent is a new platform reader of the desktop accent or wallpaper colour, which the roadmap puts in wallpaper-surfaces-consumers ("needs a Windows desktop-wallpaper seed provider"). wallpaper-foundation-and-adjust deliberately does not add it: nothing in the compiled tree would call it and a registry or wallpaper reader is platform work that needs its own review. The carried Theme.kt and PlaybackNotificationColorPolicy.kt call readSystemWallpaperSeed(context).

Wallpaper palette and media inputs the carried seed-palette, theme-chrome, favorite-search and wallpaper-foundation archives still reference after wallpaper-foundation-and-adjust. Ownership by wallpaper-surfaces-consumers is the gap author's inference: that slice's roadmap text names HomeWallpaperBackdrop.kt, WallpaperPaletteEditor.kt and SystemWallpaperSeed.kt but does not name readSeedWallpaperColorScheme, WallpaperMediaLoadState, WallpaperPaletteRequest, WallpaperPaletteResult or shouldRenderRootHomeWallpaperMedia. readSeedWallpaperColorScheme rebuilds a Material scheme from the five Android system palettes (system_accent1..neutral2 resources) and needs a Windows seed provider first. WallpaperPaletteRequest and WallpaperPaletteResult belong to the request based v0.4.6 WallpaperPaletteStore; the Windows store is a Windows-owned instance generated from v0.2.5 (extract-upstream-wallpaper-palette.py) and its consumers use the old uri/scope API. WallpaperMediaLoadState (LOADING, READY, ERROR) is declared in the Android-only v0.4.6 WallpaperMedia.kt (ExoPlayer and AndroidView); only the v0.4.6 HomeWallpaperBackdrop (which this slice does not carry) and the carried Android HomeWallpaperAdjustmentSheet, the signature reference of the Windows-owned sheet, import it, and the Windows sheet keeps its own private load state instead. shouldRenderRootHomeWallpaperMedia lives in the direct-mode HomeGlassVisualPolicy.kt and only the Root backdrop calls it (decision D9: no Root-level backdrop for every page). Its owner must confirm or reassign them when the slice is reached.

Verbatim upstream file in a carried slice archive references a symbol that no compiled, carried or vendored source declares. The producers adapt or never emit the referencing declaration today; whichever slice emits it whole must first bring the definer. No roadmap slice names this symbol yet; the owner of the first slice that emits the referencing file must assign it.

The v0.4.6 ImagePreviewDialog.kt is pinned whole in the v046-image-viewer archive, but only its pager span is consumed; the Windows preview renderer does not take the publicContent hunk. That unconsumed hunk names the public-content image loader in two places. The rss publicContent follow-up must define the loader (or route it through DesktopPublicContentImageRouting) when it applies the flag, and this gap closes with it. Ownership by rss-readability-public-network is the gap author's inference: that slice's roadmap text does not name PublicContentImageLoader.
